policy:
## Ratings / Rewards

For the initial prioritization and rating of findings, this program will use the HackerOne Vulnerability Rating Taxonomy. It's important to note that in some cases a vulnerability priority will be modified based on its likelihood or impact. In any instance where an issue is downgraded, a full, detailed explanation will be provided to the researcher — along with the opportunity to appeal and make a case for a higher priority.

---

## Credentials

Please sign up for your own accounts using your @wearehackerone.com email address.

---

## Out of Scope

Please note that we cannot authorize out-of-scope testing on third-party products or services. Vulnerabilities discovered in third-party products or services should be reported to the appropriate vendor.

The following are explicitly out of scope:

- HTML Injection
- Rate limiting
- HTTP headers without an associated, exploitable vulnerability

---

## Reporting

Please use the Report Vulnerability tab to submit a finding, or visit our partner HackerOne at [https://hackerone.com/vulnerability-rating-taxonomy](https://hackerone.com/vulnerability-rating-taxonomy).

---

## Disclosure

ASSA ABLOY Americas will follow standard industry practices for coordinated and responsible vulnerability disclosure. We ask all vulnerability reporters to do the same — please allow ASSA ABLOY Americas the opportunity to verify and remediate reported vulnerabilities and to notify affected customers and users before you disclose or share the vulnerability or exploitation methods with any third party.

ASSA ABLOY Americas product security advisories will be made publicly available at [https://www.assaabloydss.com/en/resource-center/security-center/product-security-advisories](https://www.assaabloydss.com/en/resource-center/security-center/product-security-advisories) and/or communicated directly to affected customers.

---

## Safe Harbor

ASSA ABLOY believes that ethical security research performed in good faith provides an invaluable public service and has therefore provided this safe harbor program to encourage lawful, authorized security testing of our products and services.

Accordingly, ASSA ABLOY will not initiate, pursue, or recommend any law enforcement or civil lawsuits related to the specific actions taken by you to discover a security vulnerability, provided that such actions were undertaken in good faith, for the sole purpose of improving the overall security of our products and services, and not for any nefarious or otherwise unlawful purpose.

ASSA ABLOY considers any actions undertaken in compliance with this policy to be authorized under the provisions of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, the Digital Millennium Copyright Act, and similar anti-hacking and anti-circumvention statutes. You are otherwise expected to comply with all applicable laws.

If we become aware that government authorities have initiated legal action against you for security research conducted in strict accordance with the terms of this policy, we will advise the applicable government authorities that we consider your actions to have been "authorized" hereunder.

Please note that this safe harbor policy will not apply to security activities performed in accordance with an executed, written agreement between you and ASSA ABLOY. The terms of any such agreement shall prevail in their entirety over the terms of this policy.

---

## Expectations

- Make a good-faith effort to avoid harm to ASSA ABLOY Americas, our customers, and our end-users — including, but not limited to, privacy violations, destruction of data, and interruption or degradation of our services.
- Do not access or attempt to access ASSA ABLOY Americas offices, data centers, or user accounts.
- Do not test for spam, perform phishing, conduct social engineering, or intentionally cause denial of service issues for ASSA ABLOY Americas services.
- Do not access or attempt to access our customers' or end-users' offices, data centers, or user accounts, or attempt other forms of penetration testing without the direct, written approval of the system owner.
- Comply with all applicable laws and regulations. Do not disrupt or compromise any data that is not your own, or further exploit a confirmed vulnerability.
- If a vulnerability provides unintended access to data, limit the amount of data you access to the minimum required to demonstrate a proof of concept. After ASSA ABLOY Americas validates your report, properly dispose of all copies of the data. Promptly report your findings through our approved channels.
- If at any time you have concerns or are uncertain whether your security research is consistent with this policy, please inquire via HackerOne Support before going any further.
